a: GROUP BY collapses each group into one row. A window function computes over a group of rows defined by OVER but keeps every row, so you can show detail and group values side by side.

q: Why can't you put a window function in WHERE?
a: Window functions are evaluated in the SELECT step, after WHERE, GROUP BY and HAVING. Compute it in a CTE or subquery and filter outside, or use QUALIFY in Snowflake/BigQuery/Databricks.

q: What do PARTITION BY and ORDER BY inside OVER do?
a: PARTITION BY splits rows into independent groups (the window restarts per group). ORDER BY orders rows within each group; needed for ranking, LAG/LEAD and running totals, and it also changes the default frame.
The total over the whole result set, repeated on every row. Useful for percent of total.

q: Can you use a window function over an aggregate?
a: Yes: aggregates are computed before windows, so SUM(SUM(amount)) OVER (ORDER BY month) gives a cumulative total of monthly sums, and RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(amount) DESC) ranks groups.
